Amazon Leo is Amazon’s low Earth orbit satellite network. Our mission is to deliver fast, reliable internet connectivity to customers beyond the reach of existing networks. From individual households to schools, hospitals, businesses, and government agencies, Amazon Leo will serve people and organizations operating in locations without reliable connectivity.
Amazon Leo for Government (ALG) is developing secure, high-performance satellite communications technologies that support U.S. National and International security and defense.
This role is responsible for designing, building out, and maintaining foundational software that extends Amazon Leo capabilities to U.S. Government customers such as NASA, DoD, other National Security customers, and International Government customers. You will develop brand new software services for mission critical space safety and sustainability applications which will automatically coordinate with external systems and organizations rapidly, reliably, and at scale.
You’ll work in a fast-paced, high-impact environment, tackling complex challenges in secure satellite communications. This role requires deep expertise in high-assurance, fault-tolerant software and proficiency in modern programming languages such as Rust. You’ll collaborate closely with hardware, security, systems, and product teams to develop scalable, real-time solutions tailored for government customers.
This role is based in Sunnyvale (preferred), CA, with U.S. relocation benefits available. Due to the sensitive nature of the ALG projects, onsite work is required five days a week.
This position requires that the candidate selected be a U.S. Citizen in order to comply with U.S. government-imposed requirements related to the nature of the work and/or where it will be performed.

Every flight control group, hardware owner, and mission operator depends on CDH-delivered telemetry to observe, diagnose, and act on satellite and ground appliance health.
We build and operate the systems that ingest, decode, route, and deliver telemetry from spacecraft and ground appliances to the engineers and automated systems that keep the constellation healthy. AWS Amazon Managed Prometheus is hiring!
Are you interested in building and influencing open source monitoring and observability? Would you like to use your engineering background to support best-in-class data cloud and large-scale distributed systems to enable big data processing in the cloud? We're looking for talented and driven individuals to join us.
Amazon Managed Prometheus provides a platform to AWS customers which allows them to send, store, and query metrics using the OpenTelemetry Protocol (OTLP) and Prometheus Query Language (PromQL). The AWS Managed Prometheus team builds and owns the query execution, ingestion, alerting, and long-term metrics storage systems that make this possible: the distributed query engine that evaluates PromQL expressions in real time, the storage access layer that serves reads across storage tiers, and the durable pipeline that compacts and indexes billions metric data points per day and keeps them queryable for up to 3 years. We serve customers who depend on Amazon Managed Prometheus to monitor production systems using Grafana, and other Prometheus-compatible tools. The team makes foundational architecture decisions that will shape this service for years to come. Engineers who thrive here pair strong distributed systems instincts with the discipline to build for correctness and availability at AWS scale.
Key job responsibilities
- Design, implement, and test new features across our distributed query and long-term metrics storage systems using Go, Rust and Java, leveraging AWS services including S3, Kinesis, DynamoDB, EKS, and ECS.
- Operate and maintain a globally available 24x7 service that customers rely on to monitor, alert, and analyze their metrics in real time, identifying root causes of operational issues and applying permanent fixes.
- Collaborate with customers, stakeholders, and peers to understand requirements, influence our roadmap, and shape how millions of developers and SREs monitor their systems.
- Contribute to the full software development lifecycle — from design and code reviews to testing, deployment, and documentation — while mentoring teammates through constructive feedback.
- Evaluate new tools and approaches to keep our systems and practices current, making recommendations to the team on adoption and integration.
A day in the life
On a typical day you might root-cause a customer query issue, release a new feature, consult with principal engineers on a hard architectural tradeoff, or design a solution to a storage or performance challenge you have never seen before. You translate customer requirements into designs, evaluate tradeoffs, and break work into incremental deliverables your team can ship. A strong community of principal and senior engineers gives direct feedback and pushes your thinking. You are surrounded by people who are passionate about observability and who believe there is still a lot of ground to cover in helping developers, SREs, and operators understand their systems.
About the team
The AWS Managed Prometheus team builds the query execution, ingestion, alerting , and long-term metrics storage systems behind Amazon Managed Prometheus. You’ll have the chance to contribute to open source and run a fully managed scalable service at AWS, while working with a group of incredibly smart, friendly, and passionate people.
Our mission is to give every AWS customer a reliable, performant way to store, query, and act on their metrics using open standards like OTLP and PromQL.
We invest in growing our engineers from day one — you will be paired with a buddy, work closely with senior and principal engineers, and build a personalized development plan with your manager. Our culture values knowledge sharing, constructive feedback, and an inclusive environment where every voice is heard.
Minimum Qualifications
- 3+ years of non-internship professional software development experience
- 2+ years of non-internship design or architecture (design patterns, reliability and scaling) of new and existing systems experience
- Experience programming with at least one software programming language
Preferred Qualifications
- Experience with server, storage, networking, or large-scale distributed systems
- Experience leading the design, build and deployment of complex and performant (reliable and scalable) software solutions in production
- Familiarity with time-series data, metrics systems, or the Prometheus and OpenTelemetry ecosystems
- Experience with S3-based storage, stream processing (e.g., Kinesis, Kafka), or columnar storage formats such as Parquet
- Familiarity with PromQL or other query languages for time-series data
- Experience with query planning, storage compaction, or performance optimization at scale

Amazon DynamoDB powers many of the world's fastest-growing businesses, including Lyft, Airbnb, and Redfin. It also powers enterprises such as Samsung, Toyota, and Capital One. DynamoDB is a serverless, fully managed database. It delivers consistent single-digit millisecond performance at any scale, with no servers to provision, no maintenance windows, and no downtime. We prepare DynamoDB for major events such as Prime Day and new Region launches, so capacity is in place well before customers need it. We are building fully automated capacity management from the ground up. It is a greenfield opportunity to design systems that detect, predict, and act on their own. Engineers on this team solve problems where accuracy, scale, and cost all matter at the same time, and their work shapes how customers experience DynamoDB.

- Build APIs and data platforms, that give DynamoDB teams and tools accurate, real-time views of capacity and usage.
- Reduce throttling, speed up limit increases, and make large-scale fleet events safe and predictable.

As a Senior SDE, you will set the technical direction for a cellular, multi-tenant system that runs in every AWS region.
This is a role for an engineer who wants to own hard problems end to end. You'll make the architectural decisions that determine how our failover systems behave under pressure — during regional events, network partitions, and the kinds of rare failures that most systems never have to confront. Your work directly protects the availability of the services that AWS customers, and Amazon itself, depend on every second of every day. When you get it right, no one notices; that invisibility is the whole point, and it's what makes the work so satisfying.
Day to day, you'll set technical direction across a cellular, multi-tenant platform, drive deep dives that turn operational lessons into durable mechanisms, and raise the engineering bar through design reviews, mentorship, and a relentless focus on operational excellence. You'll partner closely with product, operations, and other engineering teams, influencing roadmaps well beyond your immediate team. You won't just maintain a highly available system — you'll define what "highly available" means for the next generation of Route 53.
If you're energized by distributed-systems challenges where correctness and resilience are non-negotiable, and you want your decisions to matter at global scale, this is a place to do the best work of your career.

- Partner with customers and internal teams to deliver the resilience features they depend on, balancing short-term needs against long-term system health

We're the team responsible for failover in Route 53's DNS servers around the world—when something breaks, we make sure traffic moves away from it automatically, before customers ever notice.
